checked.title: Image method for efficiently simulating small-room acoustics
checked.correct_citation: J. B. Allen, D. A. Berkley, 'Image method for efficiently simulating small-room acoustics,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 65(4):943–950, 1979. DOI 10.1121/1.382599
checked.applicability_verdict: The citation is correct and the method fits the meeting-room case: geometry, TDOA and DRR versus distance are what matter there. Overclaim for the bus: the RT60 sweep of 0.3–0.6 s has no source. Occupied vehicle cabins are heavily damped; ETSI TS 103 224 itself treats vehicle reverberation as negligible next to a treated office. Add 0.1–0.25 s to the sweep. A shoebox ISM is specular only, so it leaves out scattering and shadowing from seats and passengers, which affect the 0.3–1 m targets most. Randomized ISM comes from De Sena et al. 2015, IEEE/ACM TASLP 23(4):774–786. My recomputation agrees with the 0.17 ms / 2.8-sample maximum TDOA at 6 cm.

checked.title: Pyroomacoustics: A Python package for audio room simulation and array processing algorithms
checked.correct_citation: R. Scheibler, E. Bezzam, I. Dokmanić, 'Pyroomacoustics: A Python package for audio room simulation and array processing algorithms,' Proc. IEEE ICASSP 2018, pp. 351–355. DOI 10.1109/ICASSP.2018.8461310; arXiv:1710.04196. PyPI 0.10.1 (2026-05-01): cp312/313/314 macOS universal2 wheels of about 1.09 MB; requires Cython, numpy and scipy; MIT-style license.
checked.applicability_verdict: Versions, wheels and API names check out: use_rand_ism (default False), max_rand_disp=0.08, return_premix with shape (n_src, n_mic, n_samples), measure_rt60 and inverse_sabine. The plan has a technical error. Source directivity works only in 3D and ISM, and the code raises NotImplementedError('Directivity not supported with ray tracing'). So 'cardioid targets plus a ray-traced late tail for RT60 0.9 s' cannot be combined. Use a high-order ISM, or add your own diffuse tail (e.g., Lehmann & Johansson 2008). The CardioidFamily patterns do not vary with frequency, which overstates voice directivity below about 500 Hz. Use the frequency-dependent measured SOFA/DIRPAT directivities (MeasuredDirectivityFile) for talkers. Ideal mics, so add self-noise and mismatch yourself; the entry already says this.

checked.title: Generating sensor signals in isotropic noise fields
checked.correct_citation: E. A. P. Habets, S. Gannot, 'Generating sensor signals in isotropic noise fields,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 122(6):3464–3470, 2007. DOI 10.1121/1.2799929. (The 2010 'Comments on…' report is unverified.)
checked.applicability_verdict: Correct and appropriate. I recomputed the coherence numbers: |Γ| = 0.5 at 4.14/2.59/1.73 kHz and first zeros at 6.86/4.29/2.86 kHz for 2.5/4/6 cm. The entry is right that the output is Gaussian only, so it is a stress test, not a realistic bus.

checked.title: Generating nonstationary multisensor signals under a spatial coherence constraint (+ Mirabilii et al. 2021 balanced/smooth extension)
checked.correct_citation: E. A. P. Habets, I. Cohen, S. Gannot, J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 124(5):2911–2917, 2008, DOI 10.1121/1.2987429. D. Mirabilii, S. J. Schlecht, E. A. P. Habets, 'Generating coherence-constrained multisensor signals using balanced mixing and spectrally smooth filters,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 149(3):1425–1433, 2021, DOI 10.1121/10.0003565. Python package anf-generator 0.1.3 (PyPI 2026-04-12, 13 KB wheel, MIT).
checked.applicability_verdict: Useful, but two implementation claims are wrong. (1) The Python code (anf_generator/MixingMatrix.py) accepts only 'standard', 'smooth', 'balance' and 'balance+smooth' (the default) and raises ValueError for 'balanced+smooth'. The entry's call with processing='balanced+smooth' would fail; 'balanced+smooth' is the MATLAB/README spelling. (2) MixingMatrix.py imports matplotlib.pyplot at module level, so installing with '--no-deps' breaks the import. Note also that CoherenceMatrix.Parameters defaults to c=340. Imposing sinc coherence on TBUS segments removes TBUS's real directional structure, such as the engine, so the output is no longer 'real bus coherence'. Use it for other spacings only.

checked.title: DEMAND: Diverse Environments Multichannel Acoustic Noise Database
checked.correct_citation: J. Thiemann, N. Ito, E. Vincent, 'The Diverse Environments Multi-channel Acoustic Noise Database (DEMAND): A database of multichannel environmental noise recordings,' Proc. Meetings on Acoustics 19, 035081 (ICA 2013, Montreal), 2013. DOI 10.1121/1.4799597. Dataset: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1227121 (v1.0, 2013-06-09).
checked.applicability_verdict: Facts checked against DEMAND.pdf: 16 Sony ECM-C10 omni electrets in 4 staggered rows, 5 cm to immediate neighbours, ±2 mm build tolerance, 21.8 cm maximum, plane parallel to the ground about 1.4 m up, 300 s per scene, recorded in Rennes 2012–13. There is no gain calibration between channels, so the per-channel equalisation step is needed. The license is CC BY-SA 3.0 in the PDF and CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo. The file sizes listed are correct. Caveats: the smallest pair is 5 cm, with no 2.5 or 4 cm pairs. OMEETING is people discussing the array, so it contains intelligible speech; label it as an interferer. Levels are not SPL-calibrated, so the dBA scaling is a choice you make. Relevance to the bus case is real.

checked.title: Estimation of room acoustic parameters: The ACE Challenge (ACE corpus)
checked.correct_citation: J. Eaton, N. D. Gaubitch, A. H. Moore, P. A. Naylor, 'Estimation of room acoustic parameters: The ACE Challenge,' IEEE/ACM TASLP 24(10):1681–1693, 2016, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2016.2577502. Corpus: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6257551 (v1 dated 2015-03-02; CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo). Corpus description: Eaton et al., WASPAA 2015.
checked.applicability_verdict: Corrections from the WASPAA 2015 corpus paper: the Chromebook (Pixel) mics are 62 mm apart, in the slot between screen and casing, just above the 2.5–6 cm range. The 3-channel 'Mobile' set (1.6 GB) has a 45 mm pair. Table 1 gives approximate dimensions and mean T60: MR1 6.6×4.7×3.0 m, 0.44 s; MR2 10.3×9.2×2.6 m, 0.37 s; Lecture Room 1 6.9×9.7×3.0 m, 200 m³, 0.64 s; LR2 13.4×9.2×2.9 m, 1.25 s. The entry missed Lecture Room 1, the only room inside the 0.5–0.9 s target. Babble came from 4–7 seated talkers reading TIMIT phrases. The eval SNRs were −1/12/18 dB. I could not verify the '1.4–4.1 m distances' or the BY-ND license note because the ACE site was down. Good for validating the simulator; not a replacement for the 20-seat sweep.

checked.title: Noise levels associated with New York City's mass transit systems
checked.correct_citation: R. Neitzel, R. R. M. Gershon, M. Zeltser, A. Canton, M. Akram, 'Noise levels associated with New York City's mass transit systems,' Am. J. Public Health 99(8):1393–1399, 2009. DOI 10.2105/AJPH.2008.138297; PMC2707461.
checked.applicability_verdict: Confirmed: in-bus Leq 75.3 dBA (SD 2.6, n=14), bus stops 76.0, highest in-bus Lmax 96.8, subway cars 79.3. Correction: the in-vehicle mean Lmax is 85.6 dBA (SD 4.7); 86.8 dBA is the combined bus-plus-stop figure. Lmax is a time-weighted level, not the instantaneous peak, and A-weighting hides engine rumble. Allow 10–20 dB of crest factor and extra unweighted low-frequency energy when checking headroom; the INMP441's 120 dB SPL AOP still makes clipping unlikely. The independent ETSI TS 103 224 'Inside Bus' recording (about 71–73 dB SPL(A) at the hands-free mic positions) supports the 70–80 dBA sweep.

checked.title: Characteristics of real-world signal to noise ratios and speech listening situations of older adults with mild to moderate hearing loss
checked.correct_citation: Y.-H. Wu, E. Stangl, O. Chipara, S. S. Hasan, A. Welhaven, J. Oleson, Ear and Hearing 39(2):293–304, 2018. DOI 10.1097/AUD.0000000000000486
checked.applicability_verdict: Numbers checked against the text: 894 situations; as noise rose from 40 to 74 dBA, speech rose from 60 to 74 dBA and SNR fell from 20 to 0 dB; 62.9% of SNRs fell between 2 and 14 dB; 7.5% were below 0 dB; median SNR was 5.3 dB for indoors crowd and 5.6 dB for traffic. The Pearsons rule (55 dBA, +0.6 dB/dB above 45 dBA, SNR 0 at 70 dBA) is correct, and Smeds is 3–5 dB higher. Wu's piecewise fit is 0.34 dB/dB below 59.3 dBA and 0.54 above. The 'Smeds speech-in-babble ≈5 dB' figure is not verified. Levels were measured at the listener's ear (Pearsons, Smeds) or chest (Wu), not exactly 1 m from the talker, and the subjects were hearing-impaired older adults. So L_s(1 m) is an approximation; the computed device SNRs of −2 to +8.5 dB are internally consistent (I re-derived them). Fine as a level prior.

checked.title: SDR – half-baked or well done?
checked.correct_citation: J. Le Roux, S. Wisdom, H. Erdogan, J. R. Hershey, 'SDR – half-baked or well done?' Proc. IEEE ICASSP 2019, pp. 626–630. DOI 10.1109/ICASSP.2019.8683855; arXiv:1811.02508
checked.applicability_verdict: Correct. The project rules (latency compensation, early-reflection reference, scoring the shadow target component) are sound. As the entry says, SI-SDR penalises the beamformer's linear colouration of the target, so report it together with ESTOI and level metrics, not alone.

checked.title: ITU-T P.862.2 Wideband extension to P.862 (PESQ-WB)
checked.correct_citation: ITU-T Rec. P.862.2 (11/2005; revised 11/2007; Corrigendum 1 10/2017). Not in force: P.862, P.862.1, P.862.2 and P.862.3 were deleted on 5 Jan 2024 and ITU refers users to P.863/P.863.1/P.863.2. Python wrapper 'pesq' 0.0.4 (PyPI, sdist only, 38.7 KB, 2022-05-17).
checked.applicability_verdict: Status and packaging confirmed. GitHub PR #59 'Add support for numpy>=2.0.0' was merged on 2026-03-18 with no PyPI release, and PR #55 pinned numpy<2 in 2024. I did not reproduce the specific 'numpy.core.multiarray failed to import' error. Agree: use it as a legacy, relative metric for near seats or the bus output only. It is not valid for two overlapping targets or far-field reverberant output. Open alternative: ViSQOL v3.

checked.title: STOI (Taal et al. 2011) and ESTOI (Jensen & Taal 2016)
checked.correct_citation: C. H. Taal, R. C. Hendriks, R. Heusdens, J. Jensen, 'An algorithm for intelligibility prediction of time–frequency weighted noisy speech,' IEEE TASLP 19(7):2125–2136, 2011, DOI 10.1109/TASL.2011.2114881. J. Jensen, C. H. Taal, 'An algorithm for predicting the intelligibility of speech masked by modulated noise maskers,' IEEE/ACM TASLP 24(11):2009–2022, 2016, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2016.2585878. Tang, Cooke, Valentini-Botinhao, Computer Speech & Language 35:73–92, 2016, DOI 10.1016/j.csl.2015.06.002.
checked.applicability_verdict: The bibliographic data is correct. I replaced the URL with the DOI because the TU Delft PDF link refused connections when I checked. pystoi 0.4.1 is an 8 KB pure-Python wheel needing only numpy and scipy, and its README states a 1e-3 tolerance against MATLAB. ESTOI is the right choice for babble. Caveats: the output is mono and the predictions are relative. Using a babble talker's ESTOI as an 'audibility' proxy mostly reflects the target-to-interferer ratio, so interpret it only as a paired change from input to output.

checked.title: DNSMOS P.835: A non-intrusive perceptual objective speech quality metric to evaluate noise suppressors
checked.correct_citation: C. K. A. Reddy, V. Gopal, R. Cutler, 'DNSMOS P.835: A non-intrusive perceptual objective speech quality metric to evaluate noise suppressors,' Proc. IEEE ICASSP 2022, pp. 886–890. DOI 10.1109/ICASSP43922.2022.9746108; arXiv:2110.01763
checked.applicability_verdict: Overclaim: the PCCs of 0.94 (SIG) and 0.98 (BAK, OVRL) are model-level, i.e., stack-ranking whole suppressors. The paper's Table 3 gives clip-level PCCs of only 0.71, 0.83 and 0.82, so per-talker or per-seat DNSMOS scores are noisy and need many clips. The model was trained on near-field DNS-challenge outputs, so far-field, reverberant 2-mic outputs are out of domain. Verified: the polynomial coefficients, INPUT_LENGTH 9.01 s with a 1 s hop, mel n_fft 321 / hop 160 / 120 mels, and model sizes sig_bak_ovr.onnx 1,157,965 B and model_v8.onnx 224,860 B. The DNSMOS README states that the personalised model (-p) penalises interfering speakers, so that part of the entry is not 'unverified'. onnxruntime 1.31.1 (2026-10-26) cp311–314 arm64 wheels require macOS 14 or later.

checked.title: A method to measure the effect of noise reduction algorithms using simultaneous speech and noise (+ Husstedt et al. 2018 multi-signal extension)
checked.correct_citation: B. Hagerman, Å. Olofsson, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 90(2):356–361, 2004. H. Husstedt, A. Mertins, M. Frenz (Marlitt), 'Evaluation of noise reduction algorithms in hearing aids for multiple signals from equal or different directions,' Trends in Hearing 22, 2018, DOI 10.1177/2331216518803198.
checked.applicability_verdict: The findings are confirmed: 5 hearing aids, up to 4 dB of noise reduction, better at positive SNR, almost ineffective at negative SNR, fast compression affects the result. Two errors in the entry. (1) The 'sanity check y+ − s_out − n_out ≈ 0' is identically zero by construction, so it tests nothing. Check polarity symmetry instead, F(−x) ≈ −F(x), or estimate the distortion term as in Olofsson & Hansen 2006, JASA 120(6):3759–3769. (2) Husstedt's linear-system method needs about K runs (a ±1 design of order ≥ K), not 2^(K−1). Overgeneralisation in the takeaways: the '≤4 dB, useless below 0 dB' result describes 2004-era single-channel hearing-aid noise reduction, not modern post-filters. Validity for DNN or mask-based black boxes is doubtful, because |S+N| ≠ |S−N| in time-frequency bins where speech and noise overlap.

checked.title: Microsoft Teams Audio Test Specification V5.0 incl. Addendum A — HEAD acoustics ACQUA 'MS Teams' (Code 60026)
checked.correct_citation: HEAD acoustics GmbH, Data sheet 'MS Teams – Measurements and Analyses According to Microsoft Teams Audio Test Specification', Code 60026, Rev. 10 (last update 05/2026), implementing the Microsoft Teams Audio Test Specification V5.0 incl. Addendum A.
checked.applicability_verdict: The data sheet confirms the test names: signal level with normal and quiet speech, idle- and active-channel SpNR, SDNR, 3QUEST S-/N-MOS under various background noises, speech level and quality for alternating near-end talkers (shared-space speakerphones), and an anechoic stage followed by a reverberant room with simulated background noise. It also confirms the basis in ITU-T P.502 and ETSI TS 103 106. 'Distractor attenuation (average and minimum)' exists only in the optional Open Office Headset module, a near-field headset test, so applying it to a far-field bus device is an adaptation. Not in the data sheet, so treat as the agent's own design: the mouth-to-mic distances (>1 m / ≤1 m) and the specific 1 m / 6 m / −8 dB / 0.5 s alternating-talker protocol. Numeric pass limits are not public. The structure is fine to reuse.

checked.title: An analysis of environment, microphone and data simulation mismatches in robust speech recognition
checked.correct_citation: E. Vincent, S. Watanabe, A. A. Nugraha, J. Barker, R. Marxer, Computer Speech & Language 46:535–557, 2017. DOI 10.1016/j.csl.2016.11.005. The secondary citation arXiv:1903.09341 is K. Shimada et al., 'Unsupervised speech enhancement based on multichannel NMF-informed beamforming for noise-robust ASR,' IEEE/ACM TASLP 27(5):960–971, 2019, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2019.2907015.
checked.applicability_verdict: Confirmed: 'with the exception of MVDR, most algorithms perform consistently on real and simulated data', and only the number of mics has a significant effect. Shimada et al. state that real-BUS WERs were 'remarkably worse' than simulated BUS and attribute this to the real bus's spatial characteristics, which supports the entry. 'Motivated CHiME-4's 1- and 2-ch tracks' is the agent's inference. The protocol lessons (inject model errors, record components separately on the real device) are sound.

missing_key_sources: ETSI TS 103 224 V1.7.2 (2026-07), 'Speech and multimedia Transmission Quality (STQ); A sound field reproduction method for terminal testing including a background noise database'. The industry 8-loudspeaker / 8-mic method with an SPL-calibrated 8-channel database (48 kHz) that includes 'Inside Bus' (about 71–73 dB SPL(A)), Cafeteria, Pub, Callcenter and Officeroom. HEAD acoustics' 3PASS, as used for the Teams spec, follows it. Files are listed at docbox.etsi.org (access not verified).

ETSI ES 202 396-1 V1.10.2 (2026-07), 'STQ; Speech quality performance in the presence of background noise; Part 1: Background noise simulation technique and background noise database'. Also 3GPP TS 26.131 / TS 26.132, the terminal acoustic requirements and test methods smartphones use to test multi-mic noise suppression.

E. Hadad, F. Heese, P. Vary, S. Gannot, 'Multichannel audio database in various acoustic environments' (MIRD), Proc. IWAENC 2014, pp. 313–317, DOI 10.1109/IWAENC.2014.6954309. Real RIRs at RT60 0.16/0.36/0.61 s, 1 and 2 m, −90° to 90° in 15° steps, with ULA spacing sets that include 3 and 4 cm pairs (spacings recalled, not rechecked). This is the closest real-RIR match to a 2.5–6 cm pair.

I. Szöke, M. Skácel, L. Mošner, J. Paliesek, J. Černocký, 'Building and evaluation of a real room impulse response dataset' (BUT ReverbDB), IEEE J. Sel. Topics Signal Process. 13(4):863–876, 2019, DOI 10.1109/JSTSP.2019.2917582. Real RIRs and noise in meeting and lecture rooms for sim-to-real checks.

Z. Chen, T. Yoshioka, L. Lu, T. Zhou, Z. Meng, Y. Luo, J. Wu, X. Xiao, J. Li, 'Continuous speech separation: dataset and analysis' (LibriCSS), ICASSP 2020, pp. 7284–7288, DOI 10.1109/ICASSP40776.2020.9053426. LibriSpeech replayed in a real meeting room with overlap ratios of 0–40%; the 7-mic circular array has about 4.25 cm pairs. Check download size against the 4.8 GB disk limit.

A. Vinnikov et al., 'NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge: New datasets, baseline, and tasks for distant meeting transcription,' Interspeech 2024, pp. 5003–5007, DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1788. Also J. Carletta et al., 'The AMI meeting corpus: A pre-announcement,' MLMI 2005, LNCS 3869, pp. 28–39, 2006, DOI 10.1007/11677482_3. Also F. Yu et al., 'M2MeT' (AliMeeting), ICASSP 2022, pp. 6167–6171, DOI 10.1109/ICASSP43922.2022.9746465. These are real multi-talker meeting recordings for sim-to-real checks.

J. Barker, R. Marxer, E. Vincent, S. Watanabe, 'The third CHiME speech separation and recognition challenge: Dataset, task and baselines,' IEEE ASRU 2015, pp. 504–511, DOI 10.1109/ASRU.2015.7404837. The primary source for the real-versus-simulated BUS data.

IEC 60268-16:2020 (Ed. 5), 'Sound system equipment – Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index' (STI). Also ISO 3382-1:2009 (C50/D50). Both are standard per-seat room-intelligibility metrics that can be computed directly from the simulated RIRs for all 20 seats.

ANSI S3.5-1997 (R2017), Speech Intelligibility Index. Also T. A. Ricketts, 'Directivity quantification in hearing aids: fitting and measurement effects,' Ear Hear. 21(1):45–58, 2000, which covers the AI-weighted directivity index (AI-DI) per ANSI S3.35. This is the hearing-aid industry's speech-weighted way to summarise 2-mic directivity, instead of narrowband MVDR numbers.

H. Cox, R. M. Zeskind, T. Kooij, 'Practical supergain,' IEEE Trans. ASSP 34(3):393–398, 1986, DOI 10.1109/TASSP.1986.1164847. The white-noise-gain / robustness constraint that governs the quoted 2-mic superdirective bounds and their sensitivity to mic mismatch.

J. M. Kates, K. H. Arehart, 'The Hearing-Aid Speech Perception Index (HASPI) Version 2,' Speech Communication 131:35–46, 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.specom.2020.05.001. Also S. Graetzer et al., 'Clarity-2021 challenges,' Interspeech 2021, pp. 686–690, DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2021-1574. These are hearing-aid industry evaluation tools and a scene-simulation protocol.

T. H. Falk, C. Zheng, W.-Y. Chan, 'A non-intrusive quality and intelligibility measure of reverberant and dereverberated speech' (SRMR), IEEE TASLP 18(7):1766–1774, 2010, DOI 10.1109/TASL.2010.2052247. A reference-free reverberation metric for far seats and real recordings.

M. Chinen, F. S. C. Lim, J. Skoglund, N. Gureev, F. O'Gorman, A. Hines, 'ViSQOL v3: An open source production ready objective speech and audio metric,' QoMEX 2020, DOI 10.1109/QoMEX48832.2020.9123150. An open alternative to the deleted P.862 family.

Å. Olofsson, M. Hansen, 'Objectively measured and subjectively perceived distortion in nonlinear systems,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 120(6):3759–3769, 2006, DOI 10.1121/1.2372591. Adds a distortion/error estimate to phase-inversion testing.

M. R. Hodgson, G. Steininger, Z. Razavi, 'Measurement and prediction of speech and noise levels and the Lombard effect in eating establishments,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 121(4):2023–2033, 2007, DOI 10.1121/1.2535571. Also A. Weisser, J. M. Buchholz, 'Conversational speech levels and signal-to-noise ratios in realistic acoustic conditions,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 145(1):349–360, 2019, DOI 10.1121/1.5087567. Also A. Weisser et al., 'The Ambisonic Recordings of Typical Environments (ARTE) database,' Acta Acust. united Ac. 105(4):695–713, 2019, DOI 10.3813/AAA.919349, whose HOA recordings can be rendered to any 2-mic geometry.

N. Alghamdi, S. Maddock, R. Marxer, J. Barker, G. J. Brown, 'A corpus of audio-visual Lombard speech with frontal and profile views' (Lombard GRID), J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 143(6):EL523–EL529, 2018, DOI 10.1121/1.5042758. Real Lombard speech for the bus targets, since LibriSpeech is read, non-Lombard speech.

E. De Sena, N. Antonello, M. Moonen, T. van Waterschoot, 'On the modeling of rectangular geometries in room acoustic simulations,' IEEE/ACM TASLP 23(4):774–786, 2015, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2015.2405476 (randomized ISM). Also E. A. Lehmann, A. M. Johansson, 'Prediction of energy decay in room impulse responses simulated with an image-source model,' J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 124(1):269–277, 2008, DOI 10.1121/1.2936367 (a cheap diffuse tail for RT60 0.9 s, since pyroomacoustics ray tracing cannot be combined with directivity).

ITU-T P.835 (11/2003), subjective test method for noise-suppression systems. Also ITU-R BS.1534-3 (MUSHRA). Also ITU-T P.56 (12/2011), active speech level, which the takeaways rely on. A small listening test is the only way to confirm 'only two talkers audible'.
verify.notes:
I found all 15 sources and kept every one. None is fabricated. Bibliographic details were checked against DOIs (OpenAlex), publisher and PMC pages, PyPI JSON, the GitHub source and the PDFs themselves. The shared web-search budget ran out late in the check, so the last items were verified by fetching known URLs and DOIs directly. These remain unverified: the ACE '1.4–4.1 m' distances and the CC BY-ND note; the exact MIRD spacing sets; the Teams mouth-to-mic distance claims; the Smeds '≈5 dB babble' figure; and the pesq/numpy-2 import error.

Corrections to apply:
(a) anf-generator: the Python option is 'balance+smooth'. 'balanced+smooth' raises ValueError, and matplotlib is imported at module level, so '--no-deps' breaks the import.
(b) pyroomacoustics: source directivity is 3D and ISM only. It throws NotImplementedError when combined with ray tracing, and the cardioid patterns do not vary with frequency. Use the SOFA/DIRPAT measured directivities and a high-order ISM or your own diffuse tail.
(c) DNSMOS: the 0.94/0.98 correlations are model-level; clip-level is 0.71/0.83/0.82. The pDNSMOS README does say interfering talkers are penalised.
(d) Hagerman: the y+ − s_out − n_out check is identically zero. Husstedt's linear system needs about K runs, not 2^(K−1).
(e) ACE: the Chromebook pair is 62 mm, the Mobile array has a 45 mm pair, and Lecture Room 1 (T60 0.64 s) is the best in-range room.
(f) Neitzel: the in-vehicle mean Lmax is 85.6 dBA; 86.8 is the bus-plus-stop figure.
(g) DEMAND: formal citation is POMA 19:035081, DOI 10.1121/1.4799597.

Physics check: I re-ran the oracle 2-mic MVDR numbers and they reproduce. Endfire gives about 5.9 dB with sensor noise at −40 dB, 1.9–4.3 dB at 250 Hz with −20 dB error, and 0.65–1.0 dB at 250 Hz in the −5 dB 'quiet meeting' case. Broadside gives 0–0.8 dB below 2 kHz. Coherence crossovers, critical distance (0.99 m), DRR, the 1.09 dB ILD and the Lombard SNRs are all right.

Overclaims and gaps:
1. The MVDR figures are narrowband, oracle-covariance, free-field upper bounds, not expected results. A ±1 dB static gain mismatch can be calibrated out, so '2–4 dB' applies only to an uncalibrated pair. Only one spatial null exists. Report speech-weighted values (SII or AI-DI weighting).
2. With two mics a source and its mirror image about the array axis are indistinguishable (cone of confusion). The bus matrix must include interferers at each target's mirror DOA as a worst case. In the meeting case several seats share a cone, so DOA-based per-talker levelling will merge them. Report per-talker results against azimuth: broadside seats get almost no directivity.
